newsitem.title: BELGIUM: US envoy fails to sway EU on anti-Cuba laws.
newsitem.headline: US envoy fails to sway EU on anti-Cuba laws.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday that Washington's Helms-Burton Act was hindering rather than helping international efforts to bring about democracy in Cuba.

After talks between European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and Stuart Eizenstat -- the special U.S. envoy appointed to win international support for Washington's anti-Cuba laws -- a spokesman said the Commission's opposition remained firm.
"We share a desire to see democracy in Cuba but the Helms-Burton Act -- objectional in principle -- does not help cooperation," the spokesman said.

Eizenstat, speaking as he left the meeting, said Brittan had "emphasised his strong opposition" to the Helms-Burton Act, an amalgamation of decades of anti-Cuba legislation signed into law by U.S. president Bill Clinton in July.
He said, however, that Brittan had promised to "reflect" on U.S. proposals to coordinate and accelerate international efforts to isolate Havana.
The EU, along with Canada and Mexico, have led international opposition to the act, part of which affects certain non-U.S. citizens or individuals doing business with Cuba.
